title: The Hollow of Ashvale Revisited
premise: Elodie Fairweather, a royal food-taster whose body has quietly absorbed three years of poison, is also a hedge-witch selling forbidden charms in Ashvale, a city where magic is punishable by ash-burning. When the crown's witch-hunt sweeps the market districts, Elodie is arrested not for his charms but because his poisoned blood makes him the only living vessel that can touch the Hollow — an ancient parasite wearing King Aldric's crown and devouring his memories. Guided by Maren Voss, a disgraced court archivist who knows the Hollow's true name, Elodie discovers the parasite feeds on inherited memory and that his own grandmother bound it once before at the cost of her identity. In the climax beneath the palace, Elodie unbinds the king by offering the Hollow his own accumulated memories of taste, love, and home, nearly erasing himself; he survives as a diminished man, magicless but remembered, while Ashvale begins reckoning with what it burned.
about_author: S. M. Crane is the pen name of a former line cook turned novelist who writes fantasy about people whose work leaves marks on their bodies. Crane lives near a harbor city that smells of brine and bread, and claims every recipe in these books has been tested, badly.

chapters.title: Salt on the Tongue
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. He tastes the king's breakfast, catalogues the arsenic, and walks home through Ashvale's charm-market where he sells a luck-knot to a fisherman's daughter. Establishes his double life and the quiet dread of being caught. Emotional beat: competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Edict Nailed to the Bakery Door
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The crown proclaims a hunt for 'the gifted,' offering silver for denunciations. His neighbor Bettina burns her own charms in the street rather than be accused. Elodie hides his stock under his floorboards. Emotional beat: fear arriving like weather, undeniable and communal.

chapters.title: What the Blood Remembers
chapters.summary: Maren Voss's POV. The disgraced archivist reads old taster ledgers and notices Fairweather's bloodwork defies records — poisons that should have killed him register as nothing. She suspects immunity is only half the story. Emotional beat: scholarly obsession sharpening into hope.

chapters.title: Charms for the Desperate
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. He keeps selling despite the edict because rent is rent, including a fever-charm for a sick child he cannot refuse. A hooded buyer watches too long from across the lane. Emotional beat: guilt braided with stubborn decency.

chapters.title: The King Who Forgets His Own Name
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. At court she observes King Aldric call his dead daughter by a servant's name and stare at his crown as if it were a mouth. The physicians whisper of melancholia; Maren suspects something older. Emotional beat: horror dressed as etiquette.

chapters.title: Denounced
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A customer he trusted — the fisherman's daughter's father — trades his name to the hunters for coin. Wardens ransack his rooms and find nothing, but they take him anyway, citing 'suspicion of constitution.' Emotional beat: betrayal landing harder than the arrest itself.

chapters.title: Cells Beneath the Mint
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In the interrogation cells he meets other accused: a midwife, a boy who whistles wind. The interrogator, Captain Rell, is less cruel than curious — he wants to know why Elodie doesn't sicken. Emotional beat: solidarity kindling in a dark place.

chapters.title: An Offer Written in Iron Gall
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren bargains with the Lord Protector: release the taster into her custody as a 'research asset' against the thing in the king. She wins, barely, and hates the arithmetic of it. Emotional beat: complicity chosen over clean hands.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Bargain
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Freed into Maren's tower custody, Elodie learns the truth: the Hollow, a memory-eating entity bound by his grandmother generations ago, wears the king. They need his blood — and his gift — to reach it. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovering your family wrote your fate.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Together they decode Elodie's grandmother's ciphered binding-notes: the Hollow can be unbound only by someone who offers it memories willingly given. The last binder lost herself entirely. Emotional beat: inheritance as both map and warning.

chapters.title: First Taste of the Hollow
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Escorted to the throne room, Elodie tastes the king's wine and feels the Hollow notice him — a cold attention like a tongue along his spine. Aldric, lucid for one breath, whispers 'run.' Emotional beat: terror laced with pity.

chapters.title: Rell's Report
chapters.summary: Captain Rell's POV. Rell files findings he knows will doom the prisoners he interviewed, then sits with the boy who whistles wind and cannot decide what duty means anymore. Emotional beat: a good soldier's conscience cracking.

chapters.title: Training the Tongue
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Maren teaches him to open his gift deliberately — reading memory-echoes in objects, tasting intention in ink. He recovers a fragment of his grandmother's voice from her ledger's binding. Emotional beat: wonder reawakening after years of hiding.

chapters.title: The Hunt Widens
chapters.summary: Bettina's POV. The market turns on itself; informers multiply, and Bettina, who burned her charms, must decide whether to shelter the midwife from the cells. Emotional beat: ordinary courage in extraordinary cowardice.

chapters.title: What the Crown Eats
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Archive research reveals the Hollow's pattern: each host king grows beloved, then hollow, then conveniently dead — and each succession strengthens it. It has ruled Ashvale longer than any dynasty. Emotional beat: scale of the horror becoming clear.

chapters.title: A Lucid Hour
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV (fragmented). Inside the remnant of himself, the king hoards small true memories — his daughter's laugh, rain on the orchard — and spends them like coins to stay himself. Emotional beat: dignity in dissolution.

chapters.title: The Fisherman's Daughter
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Wren, the girl whose father denounced him, finds Elodie to return his luck-knot and beg forgiveness. He gives it, which costs more than anger would. Emotional beat: forgiveness as a weight willingly carried.

chapters.title: Counterfeit Wards
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. To move freely, Maren forges hunter credentials using Elodie's charm-work — magic disguised as bureaucracy. Their partnership deepens into trust neither names. Emotional beat: intimacy built in conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Midwife's Testimony
chapters.summary: Bettina's POV. The midwife, smuggled out by Bettina, carries testimony of births attended by something cold in the birthing chambers — the Hollow harvesting newborn memory. Bettina takes it to Maren. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into evidence.

chapters.title: Rell Catches Them
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Captain Rell corners Elodie and Maren copying archive pages. Instead of arresting them, Rell asks one question: 'Is the king still in there?' Elodie answers honestly. Emotional beat: an enemy choosing uncertainty over certainty.

chapters.title: Preparations
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. They assemble the unbinding: grandmother's rite, Elodie's willing memories, a window when the Hollow feeds deepest — the king's midnight meal. Maren writes contingency letters she hopes never to send. Emotional beat: quiet dread before commitment.

chapters.title: The Price Named Aloud
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie finally voices what the rite requires: everything he loves remembered — his mother's kitchen, Wren's face, the taste of his own name. He may survive as a stranger to himself. Emotional beat: choosing sacrifice with eyes open.

chapters.title: Wren's Choice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren learns what Elodie intends and offers him a memory-anchor: the luck-knot, tied with her own hair, to hold a thread of him outside the Hollow's appetite. Emotional beat: love expressed as practical defiance.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Mint
chapters.summary: Captain Rell's POV. Rell's second reports the conspiracy. Ordered to seal the palace for the midnight feeding, Rell instead leaves one gate unbarred — and signs his own treason. Emotional beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Into the Palace
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Through Rell's gate, past wards that taste Elodie's blood and let him pass as 'kin to the binder.' The palace remembers his grandmother and resents him for it. Emotional beat: walking into a house that knows your name.

chapters.title: The Feeding Hour
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV (fragmented). Midnight. The Hollow draws the king's last hoarded memories up through the crown. Aldric spends his final coin — his daughter's laugh — to leave one word carved under the armrest: FAIRWEATHER. Emotional beat: a king's last act of selfhood.

chapters.title: Audience with the Hollow
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Brought before the throne as a 'gift-taster,' Elodie speaks the Hollow's true name from the ledger. The court freezes; the Hollow turns its full attention on him, curious and hungry. Emotional beat: standing unflinched before the abyss.

chapters.title: The Negotiation
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The Hollow offers a bargain: serve as its new vessel-taster and Ashvale keeps its beloved king-shape. Elodie counters with the rite — willing memories, freely offered, if it releases Aldric entirely. Emotional beat: wit and nerve against ancient hunger.

chapters.title: Maren Breaks the Seal
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Below the throne room, Maren breaks the original binding-seal in the crypt while hunters close in above. She reads her contingency letter aloud to steady her hands. Emotional beat: terror managed through ritual and stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Offering
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The rite begins. Elodie opens his memory like a pantry: his mother's kitchen, three years of tastes, Wren's face, his own name spoken by his grandmother. The Hollow feeds — and finds the memories laced with every poison he ever swallowed. Emotional beat: sacrifice weaponized.

chapters.title: Poisoned Banquet
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Three years of immunity become three years of venom: the Hollow convulses, gorged on arsenic-laced memory. Aldric's mind, freed, collapses toward death — but lucid. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from cost.

chapters.title: The King's Last Hour
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV (clearing). Restored briefly, Aldric orders the hunts ended, names Rell protector-regent, and asks Elodie whether his daughter would have known him at the end. Elodie lies kindly. Emotional beat: grace at the edge of extinction.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The Hollow, dying, tears at the palace's memory-stone; corridors forget themselves, doors open onto childhoods. Maren drags a blank-eyed Elodie out through rooms that no longer exist. Emotional beat: escape through unraveling reality.

chapters.title: Ash and Aftermath
chapters.summary: Bettina's POV. Dawn over Ashvale: the king dead, the hunts dissolved, and the city forced to look at its pyres and its informers. Bettina plants a real charm openly in the market square. Emotional beat: mourning and first light together.

chapters.title: The Man Who Tastes Nothing
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie wakes in Maren's tower with most memories gone — flavors flat, faces unfamiliar. But the luck-knot in his fist holds one warm thread: someone loved him enough to anchor him. Emotional beat: loss measured against what survived.

chapters.title: Relearning Bread
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Recovery in small acts: Wren reintroduces herself daily; Elodie retastes bread as if for the first time, because he is. Maren begins restoring his history page by page from her letters. Emotional beat: rebuilding a self from borrowed notes.

chapters.title: Trials and Testimony
chapters.summary: Captain Rell's POV. As regent, Rell convenes honest trials — including his own. Informers face the denounced; some forgive, some don't. Rell accepts his sentence without appeal. Emotional beat: accountability as the beginning of repair.

chapters.title: The Ledger Completed
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren adds the final entry to the Fairweather ledger: the Hollow unbound, the binder diminished but alive, breaking the family curse of total loss. She closes the archive and opens a school. Emotional beat: inheritance rewritten.

chapters.title: A New Charm for Old Ashvale
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Magic is decriminalized; Elodie opens a stall again, selling simple charms and teaching neighborhood children to read memory-echoes safely. Wren stands beside him. He still can't remember her face from before — but he learns it anew each morning. Emotional beat: joy chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: The Hollow of Ashvale, Revisited
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, coda. Years later, Elodie visits Aldric's grave and leaves a dish the king once tasted — safe, this time. He remembers almost nothing of who he was, yet every choice since has been made by the man the sacrifice left behind. Emotional beat: peace with an unfinished self.
